title: AstroCausal Engine: an interactive simulator of retarded-potential gravity
description:
Everything revolves around a single idea: a simulated 2D region of space in which gravitational information travels and propagates at the speed of light c. It is not a Newtonian model with causality added as a feature: it is a causal model that falls back to the Newtonian one where physics allows it, for the sake of efficiency. Each body writes its own history into multi-resolution ring buffers, and every force evaluation reads the source state back at its retarded time. On that core sit the Paczyński-Wiita pseudo-potential, 2.5PN radiation reaction in the Damour-Deruelle form and a Velocity Verlet integrator, through Numba JIT kernels, in double precision, in real time, on a consumer CPU.

The heatmaps are causal too, not only the dynamics: the value drawn at each pixel is reconstructed at that pixel's own retarded time. They cover the scalar potential and its time derivative, tidal shear, co-rotating Roche topology, Lagrange points and a projected quadrupole strain; a virtual probe records a strain series that a companion pipeline analyzes to estimate the chirp mass. In short, many of the effects you see are not imposed, but are consequences of the system.

Scope and limitations. No visualization here solves Einstein's field equations. There is no curvature of spacetime and no metric: the field is a classical one superimposed on a flat Euclidean background, under a single absolute time coordinate belonging to a distant observer. The waves are a 2D scalar analogue and a weak-field projected quadrupole, with no independent pair of polarizations. The engine runs parameter-free, with no calibration coefficients, and has been compared against public GWOSC strain data and SXS numerical-relativity waveforms; that comparison is made on instantaneous-frequency tracks, not on accumulated waveform phase, and is not of template quality. The last moments before merger, where the dynamics turn non-perturbative, are outside what the model can describe.

The author is neither a physicist nor a mathematician by trade, and the formalization would benefit from expert scrutiny. That is written with the full awareness that the work may not lend itself to it, and may remain, with dignity, in the visual and didactic realm.

Full documentation: https://github.com/alessandro-pioli/AstroCausal_Engine
